name: Seismic hazard zones
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 · Johnson et al. (2023), GEM Foundation. Adapted by GulfHazard Monitor.
method: GEM's reference-rock PGA (10% probability of exceedance in 50 years) raster clipped to the regional extent, nearest-sampled on a 0.1 degree WGS84 grid and grouped into contiguous equal-class polygons. Severity stores the lower bound of each class in g. No-data pixels omitted.

license: CC BY-NC 4.0 · Zhizhin, Ghosh, Gleason, Elvidge & Bazilian (2026), Colorado School of Mines.
method: 2025 annual site volumes (BCM) summed within 1° cells. Sites with missing or zero volume are excluded.

name: Vessel traffic
license: CC BY 4.0 · World Bank, ESMAP and PROBLUE; IMF World Seaborne Trade Monitoring System (Cerdeiro, Komaromi, Liu & Saeed, 2020).
method: Within each WGS84 1° cell, the percentage of original 0.005° cells with positive recorded AIS activity, using all original cell centres as the denominator, including land. This is spatial coverage over the entire six-year period. Cells with no recorded activity are omitted. No vessel count or transit frequency is inferred.

name: Energy & coastal infrastructure
source: NGA World Port Index · WRI · SWPC (research)
metric: Inventory records per cell or service area
metricAr: عدد السجلات في الخلية أو منطقة الخدمة
license: NGA World Port Index (public domain), WRI Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0 (CC BY 4.0). SWPC Table 1 and geoBoundaries service-area summaries are included in the research profile.
method: Ports and power plants are aggregated independently in one-degree cells. SWPC water projects are grouped by supply area. The feature source identifies the inventory and edition.

name: Subsidence & sinkholes
source: Global Urban Subsidence · Wang et al.
license: CC BY 4.0 · Wang, L., Ao, Z. et al. (2026), A global view of urban land subsidence and its changing trajectories, Nature Cities.
method: Urban study centres from Fig. 1 data. Severity is downward speed of the 5th-percentile InSAR-derived relative local vertical velocity, rounded to one decimal in mm/year. Signed Vm and V5th from the authors are retained. Points represent city-scale statistics; coverage is limited to study cities.
